ai.description: *Elaphe hodgsonii* reaches 1.5 meters. It is olive-brown with dark, irregular blotches and a distinctive black stripe behind each eye. The belly is yellowish with dark, squarish spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Elaphe hodgsonii* is best distinguished by the distinctive black "eye-stripe" that extends from behind the eye to the corner of the mouth, absent in similar colubrids.
ai.habitat: *Elaphe hodgsonii* inhabits temperate forests and rocky slopes in the Himalayas, typically ranging from 1,000 to 3,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: *Elaphe hodgsonii* is primarily diurnal and often hunts by actively foraging for small mammals and birds in both terrestrial and arboreal environments.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Elaphe hodgsonii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and early summer months in the Himalayan region.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Elaphe hodgsonii* occurs in the Himalayas across Northern India (from Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh) at elevations between 1,000 and 3,000 meters.
